To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the effects of awareness of alternative magnitude and shifts in magnitude on card sorting were not significant.

1) Ss who were unaware of alternative incentive magnitude did not sort differently from those who were aware, 2) Ss who sorted for 20 trials under one magnitude of incentive did not sort differently on Trials 21 to 27, even though the magnitude of the incentive was shifted, and 3) the magnitude of the alternative incentive did not affect the sorting behavior of Ss.
(1) neither interpretation is supported and (2) shifts in reward magnitude do not affect performance.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the effects of awareness of alternative incentive magnitude and shifts in magnitude on card sorting.
the effects of the absolute and relative magnitude of incentive and the awareness of alternative magnitudes of incentive upon performance.
the effects of incentive magnitude and shifts in incentive magnitude on performance.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the effects of magnitude on card sorting have been demonstrated, but not in the manner predicted by the authors of this paper.
the absolute and relative incentive interpretations were not supported.
neither the absolute nor the relative interpretation of magnitude is a determinant of card sorting performance.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the effects of awareness and shift on sorting are not as clear-cut as they were once believed to be.
incentive size and the interpretation of that incentive size have no effects on card sorting.
awareness of an alternative size does not influence sorting.
The main takeaway from our work is that
it is important to consider the context in which the incentive is being used.
it's not always easy to predict the effects of a shift in incentives, even in a very simple task.
the incentive used and the delivery of that incentive are important factors in the study of incentive magnitude.
